thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — we saw a perf regression on A100 clusters when seq_len > 1024. Looks like the kernel selector is falling back to a generic fp32 path instead of the BF16-optimized one.

zane: repro steps? logs? :eyes:

maria: repro is in prod canary 3. Steps: long-context chat traces + KV caching enabled. p99 token latency jumped ~40ms. Attaching probe excerpt:
```
# gpu_probe output
SM=80
TENSORCORES=1
BF16=1
FP8=0
DRIVER=525.89
PCI=Ampere_A100
```

joel: interesting — selector should pick kernel_x_bf16_seqlen_smart for SM>=80 + BF16. Could be our sequence-length policy switching to generic path for >1024 because of a safety cap.

sasha: I recall we added a conservative cutoff for caching+batching combos to avoid OOMs. Maybe that logic overrides kernel_map_v2.

perf-bot: regression alert — commit abc1234 changed kernel selection priority. p95 latency +20%, p99 +40% vs baseline.

maria: @joel can you check kernel_map priority in that commit? @sasha any ideas on KV cache interacting with kernel choice?

joel: looking now. Quick diff shows we added: `if batch_window > 64 or kv_pages > 8: force_generic` — that was meant for older GPUs. I think it doesn't account for BF16 support on Ampere.

zane: we should make the policy architecture-aware. Proposed patch snippet:
```
# pseudocode
if SM >= 80 and BF16:
  prefer = [kernel_x_bf16_seqlen_smart, kernel_x_bf16_generic]
elif FP8:
  prefer = [kernel_fp8_fast, kernel_generic_fp32]
else:
  prefer = [kernel_generic_fp32]
# only force_generic if memory_pressure && not (SM >= 80 and BF16)
```

sasha: also KV cache layout matters. When we page kv shards across GPUs the effective batch_window spikes at the scheduler level. We should measure `effective_seq_window` not raw batch_window.

maria: good point. The profiler output from canary shows high memcpy stalls right when kernel switch happens. snippet:
```
[PROFILER] memcpy_h2d_wait 12.3ms -> kernel_launch_delay 6.1ms -> runtime_kernel_generic 18.9ms
[PROFILER] when using kernel_x_bf16_seqlen_smart: memcpy_h2d_wait 5.1ms -> runtime 9.8ms
```

joel: that confirms it's strictly faster on bf16 path. We need two actions: 1) fix selector to be arch-aware and respect BF16. 2) adjust batching heuristic to use effective_seq_window and signal memory_pressure earlier.

infra-bot: FYI — adding startup probe to record SM/TENSOR/BF flags to node labels this rollout. will push label `gpu.features: sm80,bf16,tensorcores` to canary nodes.

maria: plan: I’ll open a canary PR to revert the unconditional force_generic and instead gate it. @zane can you add a unit test for selection matrix across SM+BF flags? @joel can you add a microbenchmark linking kernel_map choices to p99 number?

zane: yup, will add tests. Proposed test cases: SM=70/80, BF16 on/off, seq_len 512/2048, kv_pages 2/10.

joel: I'll run microbench on canary A100s and T4s. If results look good, we roll kernel_map_v2 to canary only then ramp.

sasha: also track memory transient when switching kernels — add a perf counter for `mem_pressure_flag` so we can correlate with kernel choice.

perf-bot: note added: perf check threshold relaxed for canary until fix is validated.

maria: thanks. I'll start the PR. tagging for awareness: @sre-team in case we need to roll back. :thumbsup: 

joel: quick follow-up — let's avoid touching quantization paths without test coverage. FP8 still flaky on older driver builds.

maria: noted. We'll keep FP8 opt-outs in the selector until drivers verified.

zane: ping when PR is up, will review fast.

maria: PR opened: https://git.redwood.internal/r/redwood/runtime/merge/PR-3482 — includes tests and canary job.

sasha: running canary perf harness now. ETA ~45m.

infra-bot: canary labels applied.

perf-bot: canary run started. baseline compare will post results here when done. :robot_face:
